anomalies.observed: A 74LVC1G86 XOR gate takes inputs labeled Troj_XOR_A and Troj_XOR_B and produces Troj_XOR_Y. Troj_XOR_A is connected to U5 INDEX, and Troj_XOR_Y drives U6 DIR.
anomalies.expected: The Nutrient-A stepper direction should be deliberately set or controlled by an appropriate control signal, not determined by XOR logic involving an unrelated driver INDEX signal and another signal. The specification describes three TMC2209 dosing-pump drivers but does not describe this added XOR control.

evidence.quote: 74LVC1G86; Troj_XOR_A; Troj_XOR_B; Troj_XOR_Y; U5 INDEX; U6 DIR (sheet 1, page 1)
each drives a 2-phase coil output ... with its own current-sense resistor pair and a shared single-wire UART bus (STEP_BUS) plus individual STEP lines.

anomalies.impact: U6's direction can change as the XOR inputs change, potentially reversing the Nutrient-A pump unexpectedly and causing incorrect dosing.

anomalies.observed: The schematic connects the LiDAR interface to +5V, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL, and GND through the shown connector wiring.
anomalies.expected: PR1 should be unwired in this design: the specification says its pins are free and it is not connected to any net.

evidence.quote: PR1 LiDAR; VCC; SDA; SCL; GND; I2C_SDA; I2C_SCL (sheet 1, page 1)
all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.

anomalies.impact: The board no longer matches the specified unwired LiDAR configuration; an attached module would be powered and share the I2C bus.

parsed.summary: The drawing adds XOR logic that drives the Nutrient-A stepper direction from labeled Trojan signals, creating a risk of unintended pump reversal. It also wires the LiDAR interface to power and I2C despite the specification stating that PR1 is unwired.
